elements.element: Transition assistance obligation on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) ... provide reasonable transition assistance"

elements.element: Assistance available for up to 6 months
Return of Customer Data within 30 days of expiry/termination (not conditioned on a request)
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days of Client's request, return to Client all Client Content and other Client data"

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format

elements.evidence: "thereafter delete such Client Content and data from its systems"
"certify such deletion to Client in writing"
"for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates" (exceeds 90 days)
"within thirty (30) days of Client's request" — the 30-day clock runs from a Client request, not from expiry/termination

reasons: The return obligation is gated on "Client's request", so the 30-day clock runs from a request rather than from expiry or termination; a request condition must not swallow the mandatory post-termination data-return duty. Change to "within thirty (30) days of expiration or termination".
Because the return trigger is request-based, the dependent deletion and certification duties ("thereafter") are also indefinitely deferred.

Duration (up to six months), then-current rates, machine-readable format, deletion and written certification are all expressly present; the format wording "commonly used, machine-readable" is substantively the standard-format requirement.
The fallback is likewise incomplete because its 30-day export element carries the same request condition, even though the 6-month assistance period exceeds the 90-day fallback.
Insertion is a concise new clause for an absent provision, changes nothing else, and introduces no undefined terms or dangling mechanics, so minimality and intent are preserved.
